alt: Handwritten definition: ambiguity in NLP is a word, sentence or phrase with multiple meanings, with the example I saw a man with telescope. Below it the five types are listed: lexical, syntactic, semantic, anaphoric and pragmatic ambiguity.
author: NLP faculty

alt: Handwritten lexical ambiguity examples: I saw a bat in a cave (flying mammal or a playing toy), He deposited money in the bank (financial bank or river bank), The bark was rough (bark of a dog or outer covering of a tree).
author: NLP faculty

alt: More handwritten lexical ambiguity examples: She fix the pitch (voice, cricket or presentation pitch), I need a new mouse (electronic mouse or small rat), They are looking at the board (piece of wood, board of directors, holding board), He dropped the glass (drinking glass or piece of glass), The athlete broke the record (musical record disk or game score record).
author: NLP faculty

alt: Handwritten definition of syntactic ambiguity: one sentence interprets multiple meanings based on sentence structure. Example: visiting relatives can be boring, either we are visiting them or they are visiting us.
author: NLP faculty

alt: Handwritten syntactic ambiguity examples with two readings each: Call me a taxi (book me a cab, or refer to me by the name of taxi), The chicken is ready to eat (cooked chicken ready to be eaten, or live chicken ready to feed), Flying planes can be dangerous (piloting the plane is dangerous, or aeroplanes that are flying can be dangerous), Look at the dog with one eye (dog with one eye, or looking with one eye).
author: NLP faculty

alt: More handwritten syntactic ambiguity examples: We need more intelligent leaders (leaders with higher intelligence, or a larger number of leaders), She hit the man with an umbrella (used the umbrella as a weapon, or hit a man who was carrying an umbrella), I shot an elephant in my pajama (I was wearing pajamas when I shot, or the elephant was in my pajamas).
author: NLP faculty

alt: Handwritten definition of semantic ambiguity: the grammatical structure is clear but the logical relationship between the words allows for multiple meanings. Examples: Someone ate every slice of pizza (one person ate the whole pizza, or for each slice some person ate it) and All students did not pass the exam (not a single student passed, or the pass rate was 70 percent).
author: NLP faculty

alt: More handwritten semantic ambiguity examples: John and Mary are married (to each other, or each to someone else) and I have not slept for 2 days (not slept for 48 hours, or slept very little in these 2 days).
author: NLP faculty

alt: Handwritten definition of anaphoric ambiguity: when a pronoun or referring expression could logically point to more than one noun previously mentioned in the text.
author: NLP faculty

alt: Handwritten anaphoric ambiguity examples: When the car crashed into the wall, it was severely damaged (the car or the wall); Mary told Susan that she had won the competition (Mary or Susan); The children ate the cake because they were very sweet (the children or the cake); Take the radio out of the car and fix it; Dad yelled at Timmy because he left the door open (Timmy or Dad).
author: NLP faculty

alt: Handwritten definition of pragmatic ambiguity: when the literal dictionary meaning of the sentence is clear but the underlying intent or goal is entirely different.
author: NLP faculty

alt: Handwritten pragmatic ambiguity examples: Do you know the time (either yes or no, or tell me the time), My coffee is cold (either a complaint or just saying), You have green light, Are you going to eat that.
author: NLP faculty
